newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Swedish finance min says Hungary on track for EU.
newsitem.headline: Swedish finance min says Hungary on track for EU.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday Hungary was in a "good position" to be accepted in the first round of EU enlargement but needed to do more to control its inflation.
"In general my observation is that Hungary is among the applicant countries which has proceeded quite far," Asbrink told a Swedish Chamber of Commerce breakfast in Budapest.
"It has carried out a successful transition and has shown impressive performance, although more needs to be done," he said.
"Just look at the Maastricht criteria...and Hungary doesn't meet these today," he said, on the second day of a two-day visit to Hungary.
"More has to be done, especially on inflation which is rather high," he said, but added: "I think Hungary is in a good position."
Asbrink, who met Hungarian Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy on Monday, said he had offered Hungary technical advice to advance its EU membership application.
"It was not so very long ago that we were an applicant country and we had to go through the same procedures," Asbrink said.

Hungary, whose inflation rate has been dropping annually but was still 18.8 percent year-on-year in March, hopes to be among the first wave of applicant countries accepted for membership by the EU when talks begin, possibly in the second half of this year.
